literal: a Finnish numeral above one governs the partitive singular, so this is right from two up and 'yksi yötä' is wrong for one -- the same trade every pack with numeral government takes, and a single form rather than the Slavic three
kello takes the bare numeral, so the slot needs no case
the Finnish shop name; a full-service pesula is a different thing

stop, please -- a bare polite-plural imperative, blunter than this pack's usual conditional requests (Voisitteko..., Saisinko...), because the concept ends the session and is deliberately not softened. lopettaa is lexically terminal against tauko in the row below, so Finnish needs no second clause where the Mandarin row carries one

a short break, please -- tauko says temporarily on its own, and unlike this pack's communication.please-wait-a-moment (Hetkinen, kiitos.) it asks the listener to suspend what they are doing rather than to wait for the speaker
do not massage this spot -- kohta is the ordinary Finnish word for a place on the body; the negative plural imperative matches this pack's laundry.please-do-not-use-bleach

a bit firmer, please -- kovempaa is the trade's word: a registered hieroja's own FAQ writes kevyemmin lupaan aina pyydettaessa ottaa, kovempaakin, jos se on mielestani tarpeen. Three words beginning Vähän against the two of Kevyemmin, kiitos, because neither button carries a labelKey on the spa board and the owner's own wording is what labels them, side by side
more lightly, please -- the other half of the trade's kovempaa / kevyemmin pair, and it modifies the therapist's ote, the grip, so it is about pressure and not speed

text: Tämä ote on hyvä, jatkakaa näin.
ipa: tˈæmæ ˈote ˈon hˈyvæ, jˈatkakaː nˈæin
literal: this grip is good, carry on like this -- ote, the grip, is what Finnish measures massage pressure in; a confirmation with a keep-it-there clause, not praise
selkä is one of the areas a Finnish hieronta price list sells by name

niska, the back of the neck, is the massage word; kaula is the throat and would be wrong here. The trade groups this with the shoulders as the niska-hartiaseutu and sells niska-hartiahieronta as one bookable service, but the two rows stay separate because a board button is one meaning

jalkaterä, the foot proper, as this pack's body-parts.foot already has it, because plain jalka would be read as the whole leg -- and jalkahieronta is a bookable service of its own in Finland rather than part of a kokovartalohieronta
right, I will leave that spot out -- Finnish has no grammatical gender, so no reply in this set needed steering

text: Tässä hoidossa sitä kohtaa ei voi jättää väliin.
ipa: tˈæssæ hˈoidossa sˈitæ kˈohtaː ˈei vˈoi jˈættæː vˈæliːn
literal: in this treatment that spot cannot be skipped -- hoito is one bookable treatment, not a hoitosarja, which would be a course of several and overstate what is being refused

I am not sure, I will ask the supervisor -- esihenkilö is the gender-neutral term that has displaced esimies, which contains mies, man; Kotus's own Kielikello and its virkakieli guidance recommend the switch
